title: Zero-Value Code Specialization via Profile-Guided Control Data Flow Analysis
problem: Zero-value propagation in programs causes redundant operations that severely impact performance. Since zero-values are generated dynamically at runtime, static analysis alone cannot eliminate these redundancies.
motivation: Modern programs frequently encounter zero-values during execution, leading to wasted computation. Traditional static optimizations miss these opportunities because zero-value patterns are runtime-dependent and application-specific.
method: ZeroSpec: A profile-guided code optimizer that combines static control data flow analysis to identify zero-value propagation patterns with runtime profiling. Uses a fine-grained cost model to evaluate optimization potential and construct targeted fast paths.
key_novelty: Efficient static control data flow analysis algorithm for identifying zero-value-induced redundancies; automated profile-guided specialization of fast paths; fine-grained cost model for optimization selection.
contributions: Static control data flow analysis algorithm for zero-value redundancy detection
Fine-grained cost model for evaluating optimization potential
Demonstration on SPEC CPU2017, NPB benchmarks
limitations: Profile-guided approach requires representative input sets; optimization potential varies by application and zero-value patterns; overhead of profiling and specialization construction.
